composition.serve_who: Drawing 108-01-520-001 Rev B is principally the vessel Bilge & Fire System: the title, pipe legend, lower flow schematic, pump data/BOM, sump pickups, bilge main, fire main, hydrants and overboard discharge all establish that service. Within the engine-room box it also shows a distinct STBD-generator raw-water loop used for emergency engine-room bilge suction; that region serves the Cummins QSB4.5 generator package and is not merged into the bilge/fire main merely because it can pump bilge water.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: This is the real system card matching the sheet title and the two drawn longitudinal mains. It receives the end-to-end operating paths and the shared roster; individual pumps, actuated valves and sensors are also attached to their own nodes below.

functions.label: Collect and discharge compartment bilge water
functions.what_it_does: Provides a sectionalized metallic suction main so the main bilge pump can dewater the selected vessel sump and discharge overboard without back-siphoning.

flow_scenarios.path: Main bilge pump stopped; normally open pickup/main isolations remain available, normally closed crossover or emergency branches pass no flow, and no sump is narrated as draining merely by gravity.

Selected drawn pickup in lazarette, midship, engine room, mast area or sail locker → its open branch isolation/check arrangement → cyan metallic main bilge line → seawater/bilge strainer at the main-pump suction → main bilge pump → discharge isolation/check route → anti-siphon manifold located 700 mm above DWL → bilge overboard.

Affected pickup or longitudinal section → closed local/section valve stops flow at that boundary; remaining pickups connected by the still-open drawn main can continue to the main bilge pump → anti-siphon manifold → bilge overboard.

key_components: sump pickup strum boxes in lazarette, midship, engine room, mast area and sail locker
branch isolation valves and non-return/check devices
functions.dry_data: Metallic main bilge line; compartment arrangement spans aft stowage/lazarette through sail locker; anti-siphon manifold elevation 700 mm above DWL.
functions.sheet_region: Lower schematic: cyan longitudinal line from LAZARETTE SUMP through MIDSHIP, ENGINE ROOM and MAST AREA to MAIN BILGE PUMP/ANTI-SIPHON MANIFOLD and SAIL LOCKER; upper GA shows corresponding hull routing.

functions.label: Provide local auxiliary and oily-bilge pumping
functions.what_it_does: Allows the engine-room and mast-area auxiliary pumps to remove local bilge liquid or draw from the explicitly piped flex/portable-oil connections, while keeping each selectable source isolated when its NC valve is shut.

flow_scenarios.path: Auxiliary pumps stopped; NC source-selector valves remain closed, so flex-hose and portable-oil branches carry no flow.

Selected drawn engine-room sump/flex-suction/portable-oil source → opened selector valve → oily-bilge filter where drawn → engine-room auxiliary bilge pump → its drawn discharge connection to the bilge piping; other NC source branches remain shut.

Selected mast-area auxiliary pickup or ESS-enclosure pickup → opened source valve on the mast auxiliary bilge-pump suction manifold → mast auxiliary bilge pump → its drawn discharge connection; unselected NC manifold branches remain shut.

key_components: two independently operated Whale auxiliary bilge pumps
ESS enclosure pickup and local bilge/coolant-leak alarms
functions.dry_data: Auxiliary line is PVC/flex per legend; two Whale Gulper 320, 24 V DC pumps, each listed 19 L/min (1.1 m³/h), 0.1 kW, max head 3 m.
functions.sheet_region: Lower center: ENGINE ROOM auxiliary-pump/oily-filter box and MAST AREA SUMP–ESS ENCLOSURE suction-manifold box.

functions.label: Pressurize the fire main and hydrants
functions.what_it_does: Uses either the electric fire pump or the independent diesel fire pump to supply the sectionalized metallic fire main and its aft and forward hydrant hose stations.

flow_scenarios.path: Fire pumps stopped; pump discharge checks prevent reverse flow and NC suction/backup branches carry no flow.

Drawn seawater supply → seawater strainer → opened electric-fire-pump suction isolation → electric fire pump → discharge check/isolation → red metallic fire main → selected aft or forward fire hydrant → hose/nozzle.

Tender-garage seawater pickup → seawater strainer → diesel fire pump (manual pull-start; fresh-water line is priming supply only) → discharge check/isolation → red metallic fire main → selected aft or forward fire hydrant → hose/nozzle.
Operating fire pump → open portion of fire main up to a closed section valve; the closed valve blocks the isolated section, while hydrants remaining on the supplied open section can receive flow.

key_components: electric fire pump and diesel fire pump as independent sources
aft and forward fire hydrant valves, 15 m hose assemblies and nozzles
fresh-water priming connection for the diesel pump
functions.dry_data: Fire hose is ISO 15540 fire-resistant; hose assemblies are shown as nominal 15 m plus 3 m; GA marks about 18 m aft-hydrant reach and 15 m forward-hydrant reach.
functions.sheet_region: Lower schematic: red longitudinal FIRE LINE from aft to forward hydrant and both pump tie-ins; upper GA: hydrant locations and dashed maximum-hose-reach arcs.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Main Bilge Pump — Gianneschi ACB 431 B
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The right-side pump labeled MAIN BILGE PUMP is the prime mover for the metallic bilge main. Established engineering resolution overrides the erroneous FEIT/VA 408 identity printed in the pump-data row: it is a separate physical Gianneschi ACB 431 B, same model as the fire pump.

functions.label: Pump selected bilge-main suction overboard
functions.what_it_does: Creates suction on the selected compartment branch and raises the collected bilge water through the protected overboard discharge.

flow_scenarios.path: Bilge main → pump stopped; no pumped discharge, with discharge check preventing reverse flow.
Selected sump pickup → metallic bilge main → suction strainer/isolation → main bilge pump → discharge check/isolation → anti-siphon manifold 700 mm above DWL → bilge overboard.

key_components: local start and remote-start controls shown on GA
functions.dry_data: Authoritative identity: Gianneschi ACB 431 B, 24 V DC, 1.5 kW, 1500 rpm; separate physical pump from the electric fire pump. The sheet’s FEIT VA 408 identity is superseded.
functions.sheet_region: Lower right, MAIN BILGE PUMP beside electric fire pump and anti-siphon manifold; upper GA near frame E/D with local and remote starts.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Auxiliary Bilge Pumps — engine room and mast area
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The two local pumps labeled E-R AUX BILGE PUMP and MAST AUX BILGE PUMP match the established two-unit Whale Gulper 320 auxiliary set.

functions.label: Pump locally selected auxiliary bilge source
functions.what_it_does: Each pump independently evacuates the source selected by its own drawn suction valves/manifold; neither pump is assumed connected to a source lacking a drawn pipe.

flow_scenarios.path: Pump stopped; NC selector branches remain shut and pass no flow.
Selected engine-room/flex/portable-oil branch → opened isolation and oily-bilge filter where drawn → engine-room Whale pump → drawn discharge connection.
Selected mast-area or ESS pickup/flex/portable-oil branch → opened mast suction-manifold valve → mast-area Whale pump → drawn discharge connection.

key_components: local alarms associated with the served sumps
functions.dry_data: BOM 003: Central Boating / Whale 2054 Gulper 320, 24 V DC, quantity 2; each 19 L/min (1.1 m³/h), 0.1 kW, max head 3 m.
functions.sheet_region: Lower center-left E-R AUX BILGE PUMP and lower center-right MAST AUX BILGE PUMP; upper GA shows both remote-start locations.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Electric Fire Pump — Gianneschi ACB 431 B
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The electric motor-driven fire pump is shown as a separate physical pump connected between the seawater suction arrangement and fire main; established identity explicitly prevents merging it with the same-model main bilge pump.

functions.label: Electrically pressurize the fire main
functions.what_it_does: Provides the normal electric pumping source for fire-fighting water at the vessel hydrants.

flow_scenarios.path: Seawater suction → pump stopped; discharge check prevents fire-main backflow through the pump.
Drawn seawater supply → seawater strainer → open suction isolation → Gianneschi electric fire pump → discharge check/isolation → metallic fire main → selected hydrant → hose/nozzle.

key_components: local/remote pump controls shown on GA
functions.dry_data: BOM 024: Gianneschi S.r.l. ACB 431 B, 24 V CC, 1.5 kW, 1500 rpm (SWS GIA-01AAC9991); pump table lists 230 L/min (13.8 m³/h), max head 30 m.
functions.sheet_region: Lower right-center ELECTRIC FIRE PUMP branch; upper GA near frame D with pump and remote-start symbols.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Diesel Fire Pump (crash/backup pump) — Aussie Pumps / Yanmar L48
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The tender-garage manual pull-start pump is the independent diesel fire-main source and is labeled on the GA as both diesel fire pump and diesel backup bilge pump.

functions.label: Independently pressurize the fire main
functions.what_it_does: Provides a manually started, engine-driven fire-water source independent of the 24 V electric fire pump.

flow_scenarios.path: Tender-garage seawater pickup → pump stopped; discharge check prevents reverse flow from the fire main.

Tender-garage seawater pickup → seawater strainer → open suction isolation → manually pull-started diesel pump → discharge check/isolation → metallic fire main → selected hydrant → hose/nozzle; the fresh-water branch from drawing 108-01-510-001 is used for priming, not treated as the pump discharge.

Bilge pickup/backup suction route shown at the tender-garage branch → required NC selector opened → diesel pump → drawn bilge-overboard route; the normal seawater/fire lineup must not be assumed open through an NC selector.

functions.dry_data: Register/BOM identity: Aussie Pumps RSEBUV/L48 NF driven by Yanmar L48; pump table lists 715 L/min (42.9 m³/h), 5.6 kW, max head 37 m.
functions.sheet_region: Lower left TENDER GARAGE boxed branch; upper GA aft near lazarette/tender garage with diesel fire-pump and backup-bilge labels.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Bilge Valves — Burkert electric actuated set and manual isolations
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The sheet uses valves to select sump suction, isolate sections and prevent reverse flow. The established BOM mapping identifies the five electric-actuated DN50 bilge ball valves; the remaining drawn manual/check valves are retained by role without inventing actuator links.

functions.label: Select and isolate bilge-flow paths
functions.what_it_does: Opens the commanded pickup or pump route while isolating unused branches and preserving one-way discharge protection.

flow_scenarios.path: Valves marked NO remain open on their drawn branches; valves marked NC remain closed and carry no flow; check valves permit only the arrowed pumping direction.
Chosen sump/source → commanded Burkert or manual isolation opened → connected drawn main/manifold → operating pump; all unselected NC branches remain shut.
Affected pickup, pump or main section → adjacent isolation closed → flow blocked at that valve while other independently piped open sections remain available.

key_components: five electrically actuated 2-way DN50 ball valves
functions.dry_data: BOM 016+017: Burkert electric rotary actuators on Burkert 2-way 316 stainless DN50 ball valves, quantity 5; 24 V supply is established elsewhere via Q14 10 A emergency-panel breaker.
functions.sheet_region: Distributed across the lower bilge main, pump branches and mast auxiliary suction manifold; motor-actuated-valve symbols are defined in the lower-left legend.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Vega bilge level sensors / bilge alarm points
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Bilge alarm points are drawn in the lazarette, midship, engine-room, mast-area, ESS and sail-locker sump boxes and belong to the bilge monitoring equipment rather than to the pumps.

functions.label: Detect abnormal liquid level in local sumps
functions.what_it_does: Provides a local level/alarm input at each depicted bilge area so accumulation is indicated independently of pump operation.

flow_scenarios.path: Sump level below sensor trip point → sensor remains normal → no bilge alarm indication.

Liquid rises at the local sump sensor → level switch changes state → associated bilge alarm indication shown for that compartment; no automatic pump-start relationship is asserted because this fluid sheet does not draw such control wiring.

key_components: bilge alarm annunciation points 007-01 through 007-06 as drawn
separate auxiliary-pump and coolant-leak alarm symbols where shown
functions.dry_data: Vega bilge-level-sensor family; exact BOM quantity/model-to-each-alarm-point mapping is not cleanly legible on this image and is not inferred.
functions.sheet_region: Bottom sump boxes for LAZARETTE, MIDSHIP, ENGINE ROOM, MAST AREA, ESS ENCLOSURE and SAIL LOCKER.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: STBD Generator Cummins QSB4.5 raw-water pump / emergency bilge suction
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The boxed engine-room branch explicitly references sea-chest supply and wet-exhaust water separation and contains the established STBD generator Jabsco 43400 pump. It is a separate generator raw-water loop with an emergency bilge selector, not a branch merged into the fire main.

functions.label: Supply raw water to the STBD generator wet-exhaust circuit
functions.what_it_does: Pumps seawater through the generator cooling/exhaust-water route during ordinary generator operation.

flow_scenarios.path: Main sea-chest supply referenced to drawing 108-01-515-003 → open normal suction route → STBD generator Jabsco 43400 raw-water pump → wet-exhaust water separator → overboard route referenced to drawing 108-01-515-001; emergency bilge suction valve remains NC.
Raw-water pump stopped → no pumped seawater circulation; emergency bilge suction remains closed.

functions.dry_data: Jabsco 43400 engine-mounted raw-water pump on STBD Cummins QSB4.5 generator; sheet pump table lists 195 L/min (11.7 m³/h).
functions.sheet_region: Lower-center dashed ENGINE ROOM box, left side: FROM SEACHEST SUPPLY and STBD GENSET RAW WATER PUMP to overboard wet-exhaust reference.

functions.label: Use the generator raw-water pump as emergency bilge pump
functions.what_it_does: Allows the STBD generator pump to draw from the engine-room bilge instead of its normal sea-chest suction during flooding.

flow_scenarios.path: Emergency engine-room sump suction → NC emergency selector closed → no bilge flow into generator raw-water pump.

Engine-room bilge pickup → emergency suction valve opened and normal sea-chest lineup isolated as required → STBD generator Jabsco 43400 raw-water pump → exhaust water separator → overboard; this is the established emergency engine-room flood-suction route.

functions.dry_data: Emergency alternate suction on the STBD generator raw-water pump; no independent gravity discharge is claimed.
functions.sheet_region: Lower-center ENGINE ROOM box around the STBD GENSET RAW WATER PUMP and emergency pickup branch.

infrastructure.system_name: Bilge & Fire System shared piping infrastructure
facts: The cyan metallic main bilge line and red metallic fire main are separate longitudinal networks; common vessel routing does not make them one pipe.
The bilge main is sectionalized across hull/fire boundaries and receives only pickups with a drawn branch: lazarette, midship, engine room, mast area and sail locker.
The auxiliary PVC/flex piping and mast suction manifold remain distinct from the metallic main except at explicitly drawn connections.
The fire main is sectionalized and supplies aft and forward hydrants; either electric or diesel fire pump can feed it through its own drawn check/isolation branch.
Aft and forward hose/nozzle stations are each shown with nominal 15 m plus 3 m hose arrangement; upper GA gives the coverage arcs.

Cross-sheet boundaries are explicit: fire line in port sheet and sea-chest supply refer to 108-01-515-003; fresh-water priming to 108-01-510-001; wet-exhaust overboard route to 108-01-515-001; thru-hull valve details to 108-01-504-002.

Shared roster on this sheet includes main bilge pump, two auxiliary bilge pumps, electric fire pump, diesel fire pump, sump pickups/alarms, oily-bilge filter, strainers, hydrants, valves/checks and anti-siphon manifold.

discarded_as_clutter: revision-history wording except the functional fact that Rev B added the ESS pickup
standard drafting notes such as DO NOT SCALE, dimensions and edge-breaking
upper-GA repeated pump/start labels already represented by the lower flow schematic
symbols-legend repetitions after applying the sheet’s symbol meanings
pipe-detail and BOM weight columns that do not change operational function
zone letters, frame numbers, room furniture and hull outlines used only for drawing location
vendor material/weight details for hoses and minor fittings where they merely repeat the fire-hose specification
cross-reference arrows treated as off-sheet boundaries rather than invented connections
uncertainties: The main bilge pump’s printed FEIT VA 408 row and its listed 300 L/min, 0.75 kW, 17 m performance conflict with the engineer-resolved Gianneschi ACB 431 B identity. Identity is closed; applicability of those three printed performance values after correction is not established, so they were not adopted.

The exact item/model and quantity mapping of each 007-series bilge alarm point to the Vega BOM row is not cleanly readable at this image resolution; six compartment alarm positions are drawn, but no quantity is guessed.

The auxiliary pump discharge endpoints are visibly connected into the depicted bilge piping, but some tiny valve/item identifiers and arrowheads are not legible enough to assign every tag; paths are therefore stated by functional branch rather than guessed tag number.

The precise valve sequence for the diesel pump’s GA-labeled backup-bilge mode is not fully legible on this sheet; the scenario is limited to the drawn backup suction/overboard branch and does not assert flow through any valve marked NC unless explicitly opened.
The drawing refers to separate operating-modes sheet 108-01-520-002; any interlocks or mandatory sequencing shown only there are outside this sheet and are not inferred.
